channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Bishkek Police Arrest Suspects in $1 Million Robbery, Recover Stolen Funds
item.description: Bishkek police have arrested several suspects in connection with a robbery where foreign national lost nearly $1 million. The incident occurred on November 17, with four individuals allegedly using a firearm to steal a bag containing $988,500, 200,000 soms, phones, and a passport. Investigations led to arrests in Bishkek and a neighboring country, with over $810,000 recovered.

item.title: Eurasian Development Bank to Invest $500 Million in Uzbekistan Projects by 2027
item.description: The Eurasian Development Bank (EDB) plans to invest at least $500 million in Uzbek projects in 2027. This was discussed during a meeting between EDB Chairman Nikolay Podguzov and Deputy Prime Minister Jamshid Khojaev, who also reviewed the bank's Country Strategy for 2027-2031. Priority areas include transport, water and energy, industry, digitalization, and SME support.

item.title: International Sports Complex 'Tсор' to be Built on Issyk-Kul Lake
item.description: An international sports complex named 'Tсор' is planned for construction in the Issyk-Kul region of Kyrgyzstan. The facility will accommodate training for 40 Olympic sports and is estimated to cost $30-50 million. The project, deemed of state importance, will be developed under a public-private partnership, with the land already allocated to the Tourism Development Fund.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Lawmaker Proposes Rehabilitation Centers and School Tutors for Disabled Children
item.description: A member of the Kyrgyz parliament has proposed establishing rehabilitation and diagnostic centers in every district and integrating children with disabilities into mainstream schools with the support of specialized tutors. The initiative aims to address the growing number of individuals with disabilities and improve access to medical care, rehabilitation, and education, regardless of location.

item.title: Ala-Too Resort Ski Center to Open, Expecting 15,000 Tourists
item.description: The official international opening of the Ala-Too Resort mountain ski center is scheduled for December 1st, with approximately 15,000 tourists expected to attend. Preparations for the opening and the UN International Tourism Forum on December 3-4 were discussed at a meeting of the State Agency for Tourism Development.

item.title: Zelensky Rejects Lukashenko's Proposal for Joint Trip to Moscow for Talks
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky sharply criticized Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko's proposal for a joint trip to Moscow to negotiate with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Zelensky stated that meeting in Moscow or Kyiv is not possible due to the ongoing war and questioned Lukashenko's offer to accompany him.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP Proposes 1 Billion Som Loan Program for Women Farmers
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kyrgyzstan has proposed allocating 1 billion som to a loan program aimed at supporting women in agriculture. The initiative, timed with the UN's declaration of 2026 as the International Year of Women Farmers, seeks to address financial and land access challenges faced by women in the sector.

item.title: Kazatomprom Top Manager Detained Amid Corruption Probe
item.description: Kazatomprom's Chief Operating Officer for Production, Kuanysh Omarbekov, has been detained on suspicion of involvement in a corruption scheme allegedly organized by the former leadership of the Samruk-Kazyna fund. The national security committee confirmed the detention, with other individuals also apprehended.

item.title: Ex-Son-in-Law of Karim Masimov Requests Case Transfer from Financial Monitoring Agency
item.description: Azamat Kapenov, former son-in-law of Karim Masimov and ex-vice president of KazTemirTrans, has appealed to President Tokayev to transfer his criminal case from the Financial Monitoring Agency (AFM) to the National Security Committee (KNB). Kapenov claims the KNB is less corrupt and seeks an audit to prove no financial damage was caused.

item.title: Kazakhstan Operates Approximately 180 Dental Clinics in Schools
item.description: Around 180 dental clinics are operational in Kazakhstan's schools. The Ministry of Health continues efforts to improve access to dental care for students. This was announced by the acting Minister of Health, Timur Sultanğaziyev, during a plenary session. Currently, over 7,000 schools have functioning medical points.

item.title: National Security Committee Confirms Arrest of Kazatomprom Top Manager
item.description: The National Security Committee (KNB) has confirmed the arrest of a top manager at Kazatomprom, the national atomic company. Further details regarding the individual and the reasons for the arrest have not yet been disclosed by the authorities.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Fixed Capital Investments Reach 422 Billion Som in 10 Months
item.description: In the first 10 months of 2026, Kyrgyzstan's fixed capital investments reached 422 billion som, contributing to a 10.5% real growth in GDP. The government is prioritizing the development of industry, agriculture, energy, and transport logistics, including the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Health Ministry opposes pausing electronic queues in polyclinics
item.description: A member of Uzbekistan's Legislative Chamber proposed temporarily halting the electronic queue system in family polyclinics, citing infrastructure issues and patient inconvenience. He suggested a pilot test in a single facility. The Health Ministry, however, opposed the pause, emphasizing the system's benefits for patient flow and accessibility.

item.title: US warns citizens in Middle East of increased Houthi and Iran threats
item.description: The US Department of State has issued a security warning for American citizens in the Middle East, citing an increased threat of armed attacks by Iran-backed Houthi forces and Iran's attempts to target US officials and facilities. The warning advises citizens to stay informed about potential security alerts and travel disruptions.

item.title: Kazatomprom Dismisses Two Top Commercial and Production Directors Amid Corruption Probe
item.description: Kazatomprom has terminated the powers of its Chief Commercial Director Vladislav Baiguzhin and Chief Production Director Kuanysh Omarbekov. The decision was made on November 24, following the detention of Omarbekov and others on November 23 for suspected involvement in a corruption scheme. The company assures that business operations continue as usual.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Health Minister Cites Funding Issues for Delays in Free Medical Treatment Referrals
item.description: Uzbekistan's Minister of Health, Eldor Adilov, stated that delays in obtaining referrals for free planned inpatient treatment are primarily due to funding issues. He addressed parliamentary concerns about difficulties in accessing specialized medical centers, attributing the problem to disruptions in financing from the State Medical Insurance Fund, not digitalization.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prepares New Law to Protect Medical Data and Ensure Transplant Transparency
item.description: Kazakhstan is introducing legislative changes to digitalize healthcare and enhance patient data security. The bill grants citizens digital access to their health information and electronic informed consent for procedures. It also regulates AI use in medicine, emphasizing its role as a support tool for doctors, and strengthens accountability for medical professionals.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Expand Bitumen Storage Capacity by 2.5 Times for Road Construction
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Transport plans to increase the total capacity of five bitumen storage bases by 2.5 times, from 13,500 to 33,800 tons. This expansion aims to ensure a stable supply of materials for road construction projects. The modernization program includes installing new equipment and building additional reservoirs, with the largest expansion at the Shamaldy-Say base.

item.title: UNHCR Reports Over 1.3 Million Afghan Migrants Returned Since 2026
item.description: The UNHCR states that more than 1.3 million migrants have returned to Afghanistan from Iran and Pakistan since the start of 2026. Many returnees have limited resources and require immediate assistance. The agency is providing aid and emphasizes the need for long-term support for reintegration.

item.title: Bishkek School No. 37 Plans Expansion with New Building and Sports Facilities for 337 Million Som
item.description: The capital's capital construction department has announced a tender for the construction of a new three-story building and sports facilities for School No. 37 in Bishkek. The estimated cost of the project is 337.8 million som. The expansion includes classrooms, sports fields, and landscaping.

item.title: Kazatomprom Dismisses Two Board Members Amid Corruption Investigation
item.description: Kazatomprom has prematurely terminated the powers of two board members, Vladislav Baiguzhin and Kuanysh Omarbekov, amidst an ongoing corruption investigation. The National Security Committee confirmed Omarbekov's detention in connection with a scheme allegedly organized by former Samruk-Kazyna leadership.

item.title: Former Head Doctor Sentenced to 8 Years for Embezzling Hospital Funds
item.description: A former head doctor and a businessman in the Turkistan region have been sentenced for embezzling 117 million tenge allocated for medical equipment. They allegedly inflated prices for oxygen systems, defrauding the state. The former head doctor received an 8-year sentence, and the businessman received 7 years. Assets including an apartment and two cars were confiscated.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Stricter Energy Consumption Controls for Public Institutions
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering new legislation to enhance control over energy consumption in schools, hospitals, and kindergartens. The proposed amendments aim to reduce the country's GDP energy intensity, which remains significantly higher than global averages. The measures are crucial for energy security and economic stability amid global energy transitions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes New Method to Reduce Drug Prices Through Simplified Registration
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a proposal to register different dosages of the same drug under a single procedure, rather than separate registrations. This aims to reduce costs for manufacturers and suppliers, speed up market entry, and lower drug prices. The Ministry of Health supports the initiative, noting current registration times have been reduced.

item.title: Pakistan's Ambassador to Russia raises security concerns over Afghanistan
item.description: Pakistan's Ambassador to Russia stated that countries outside the region are using Afghan territory to destabilize Pakistan. He expressed concerns about the security situation and cross-border activities.

item.title: Baiterek Holding to allocate 4.1 trillion tenge for business lending via banks
item.description: Baiterek Holding announced plans to allocate 4.1 trillion tenge to support business lending through commercial banks. This initiative aims to boost economic activity and provide financial resources to enterprises.

item.title: Switzerland to Return Another $252.5 Million in Illicit Assets of Gulnara Karimova to Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan and Switzerland have agreed to return another tranche of illegally acquired assets belonging to Gulnara Karimova, totaling $252.5 million. The funds will be channeled through the 'Ishonch' trust fund and allocated to social programs, focusing on healthcare and education. This follows a previous return of $87 million in the first phase of the restitution strategy.

item.title: Kazakh National Security Committee Arrests Kazatomprom Top Manager in Samruk-Kazyna Corruption Case
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) has arrested Kuanych Omargbekov, a board member of Kazatomprom, as part of a corruption investigation into Samruk-Kazyna. He and others were detained on November 23 and placed in a temporary detention facility, suspected of involvement in a corruption scheme organized by former Samruk-Kazyna leadership.

item.title: Kazatomprom Director Detained on Suspicion of Corruption Involvement
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee detained Kuat Omarbekov, a board member and chief production director of Kazatomprom, on suspicion of involvement in a corruption scheme. He is suspected of bribery. This follows the earlier detention of the heads of Samruk-Kazyna and Kazakhstan Temir Zholy for alleged corruption offenses.

item.title: Osh Region to Strengthen Measures Against Construction Law Violations
item.description: The Osh region in Kyrgyzstan will intensify state supervision over construction sites to ensure timely measures against violations. The Ministry of Construction announced that inspectors must strictly monitor compliance with project documents, building codes, and safety requirements. Body cameras and anti-corruption measures are mandated for inspectors.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Enhance Control Over Energy and Heat Consumption
item.description: Kazakhstan will strengthen control over the consumption of electricity and heat through amendments to energy-saving and energy-efficiency legislation. The changes propose lowering the threshold for mandatory energy-saving agreements for businesses and increasing oversight of data submitted to the state energy registry. Budgetary organizations will face new monitoring requirements.

item.title: Kazakhstan to enable remote medical image analysis by doctors nationwide
item.description: Kazakhstan is introducing a system to unify X-ray, CT, and MRI results, allowing doctors in different clinics to remotely study medical images. This initiative, part of healthcare law amendments, aims to improve the quality and accessibility of medical care by facilitating information exchange between regional and national medical centers.

item.title: Nearly 80% of Kazakh companies use loans for current expenses, not expansion
item.description: A survey by the National Bank of Kazakhstan reveals that almost 80% of companies receiving bank loans use them for working capital and current expenses, with only 1.3% investing in business expansion. The average loan interest rate in tenge is 18%, significantly higher than the 7.9% deemed acceptable by businesses.

item.title: Central Asian Corporate Governance Alliance to be established on Kyrgyzstan's initiative
item.description: Professional organizations from Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan have signed a protocol to establish the Central Asian Corporate Governance Alliance. Initiated by Kyrgyzstan's Chamber of Independent Directors, the alliance aims to harmonize regional corporate governance standards, develop specialists, and foster market growth for independent directors.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee Detains Board Member of Kazatomprom
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) has detained Kuanych Omarbekov, a board member of Kazatomprom, and other individuals. They are suspected of involvement in a corruption scheme organized by the former leadership of Samruk-Kazyna. A pre-trial investigation is underway.

item.title: Almaty Mountain Tourism Cluster Development Enters Implementation Phase
item.description: The development project for Almaty's mountain cluster has moved from the design to the implementation stage. Work is underway at Shymbulak and Oi-Qaragai resorts, and Almaty SuperSki construction is progressing. A unified year-round mountain resort system is being formed.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Turkey to Exchange Experience in Election Organization
item.description: Turkey's Supreme Election Council Chairman Serdar Mutta expressed readiness to participate as an international observer in Kyrgyzstan's 2027 presidential election. The statement was made during a meeting with Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission Chairman Tynchtyk Shainazarov, where cooperation and experience exchange were discussed.

item.title: Kazakh Scientists Explore New Avenues for Cancer Treatment
item.description: Specialists from Kazakhstan's National Scientific Oncology Center, in collaboration with Nazarbayev University, are investigating why tumor cells become resistant to chemotherapy and how to improve treatment effectiveness for bladder cancer patients. Local media reported the findings, citing the Ministry of Health of Kazakhstan. The study involves approximately 60 patients and utilizes advanced 3D cell models.

item.title: Kyrgyz Lawmaker Proposes Special Schools for Children with Disabilities
item.description: Member of Parliament Zhanybek Abirov suggested opening special schools for children with disabilities in Bishkek. He noted that as of May 2026, 5,000 children with disabilities are registered in Bishkek, with only three municipal auxiliary schools available. Private schools are too expensive for many parents, leaving some children without education and social integration. Abirov also emphasized the need for inclusive education in regular schools.

item.title: Turkistan Region Enhances Student Safety with Over 11,000 Cameras
item.description: The Turkistan region is significantly enhancing student safety by installing over 11,158 digital surveillance cameras across 915 general education schools, covering both internal and external areas. This initiative aligns with the 'Children of Kazakhstan' program and aims to ensure a secure learning environment. The measures include updating technical security systems in educational institutions, with a focus on anti-terrorism protection.
